Question: If the world is overpopulated and unsustainable, why are people suggesting the population decline is a bad thing?
Answer: Split the population into two categories: In this terminology, “producers” are people who create more than they consume, and “consumers” are people who consume more than they create. In that sense, you can batch up the population into three broad sections: It actually doesn’t matter how your measuring production providing you’re using the same measurement for consumption. Clearly, this is a simplification, because there are lots of working age people who aren’t producers - everyone from critically disabled people to trust fund babies. But actually, it turns out the simplification is good enough. Population decline Isn’t really happening because all three groups are shrinking. It’s happening in a way that means lots of people are getting older but not being replaced by equivalent numbers of younger people. There is a limit to how many consumers a society can support. If there were three producers for every consumer in a society, then that implies a certain ability of that society to support living conditions for its consumers. If, however, the population changes in a way that there are a lot more retired people per working age person, this is kind of good, because it means people are living longer, but kind of bad because it means each producer might need to support a whole consumer on average, rather than just one third of a consumer. Advances in technology can lead to advances in productivity, so actually the situation doesn’t get worse as fast as you might imagine… Shrinking population tends to mean there are far fewer children. So we can see that, in 10 to 20 years time, there will be fewer working-age people.

Question: Why does Bill Gates think that Tesla’s electric semi-trucks and airplanes will never work?

What the last 10 years have taught is that actually that’s far less of an issue for most people then we all imagined it would be. There are alternative methods that evolve quick removal batteries, that can be replaced by fully charged ones. For a big logistics company that has thousands of trucks on the road at any given time, setting up a series of batteries swap depot feels like a better solution than multi hour charging cycles.
